questions.scenario: Your best friend is going through a terrible breakup and is crying uncontrollably. How do you help?

options.text: Sit with them for hours, listen without judging, and create a safe space for them to process their deep emotions.
Explain how a sudden drop in dopamine and oxytocin is causing the pain, and suggest a scientific routine to fix their sleep and mood.
Gently distract them, reassure them that this is a normal part of growing up, and keep an eye on them during school hours.
Organize a massive, highly-planned group outing with your entire friend circle to completely divert their mind and boost morale.

questions.scenario: Board exams are approaching, and the entire class is having collective panic attacks. What is your reaction?

options.text: Start a deep 1-on-1 support chain where friends can call you at night to talk about their deepest fears of failure.
Read up on neuroscience to find the absolute best sleep-cycle and diet to maximize brain retention and reduce cortisol (stress hormone).
Host a calm 'stress-buster' circle during the free period, giving everyone practical tips on handling exam anxiety.
Create a master study group system, matching the class toppers with the strugglers so the whole group succeeds efficiently.

questions.scenario: There is a massive sibling fight at home over who gets to sleep in the AC room during peak summer. How do you step in?

options.text: Mediate a deep conversation to figure out if one sibling feels 'less loved' or ignored, fixing the root emotional issue.
State the biological facts about how the human brain needs lower temperatures for better REM sleep, ending the argument with science.
Gently guide them to a fair compromise where both feel heard, like splitting the week into 3 days and 4 days.
Set up a strict 'reward system' where the sibling who does more household chores (like filling water bottles) earns the AC room.

questions.scenario: You notice a quiet kid in your class sitting alone during the lunch break every single day.

options.text: Sit next to them, ask gentle open-ended questions, and let them vent about their feelings if they want to.
Observe their body language and signs to see if it's just shyness or a deeper issue like clinical social anxiety.
Slowly introduce them to your friend group over a few weeks, making sure they feel included without overwhelming them.
Notice that the class seating arrangement is flawed and suggest the teacher rotate desks so everyone is forced to interact more.

questions.scenario: Your uncle and aunty are forcing your cousin to take Science (PCM), but your cousin desperately wants to study Arts.

options.text: Help your cousin uncover their true inner passion and build the emotional courage to stand up for themselves.
Research the biological stress levels and burnout rates of forced careers to present a highly logical argument to the parents.
Act as the perfect middle-man, sitting with both your cousin and the parents to facilitate a peaceful, calm discussion.
Help your cousin build a professional 'pitch' showing the financial viability and high-paying jobs available in the Arts field.

questions.scenario: You decide to do a 'Social Media Detox' and delete Instagram for a week. What is your primary reason?

options.text: To reconnect with your own thoughts, journal your feelings, and heal your inner self from comparison.
To scientifically reset your brain's dopamine receptors and prove that you can cure your own shrinking attention span.
To set a good, healthy example for your younger sibling who is getting way too addicted to scrolling reels.
To test if removing distractions naturally increases your daily productivity and time-management skills.

questions.scenario: It's a group project, but nobody is doing their work and everyone is arguing on the WhatsApp group.

options.text: Call each member individually to understand what personal problems or insecurities are stopping them from contributing.
Diagnose the group's 'pathology'—realizing that sheer exhaustion, sleep deprivation, and caffeine are causing the irritability.
Call a peaceful 'circle time' meeting, clear the air, and rebuild the team spirit with positive reinforcement.
Completely restructure the team, reassigning roles based on exactly what each person is naturally best at doing.

questions.scenario: You are watching a dark psychological thriller movie (like Bhool Bhulaiyaa or Drishyam). What are you analyzing?

options.text: Trying to deeply understand the tragic childhood backstory and emotional trauma that made the villain act that way.
Pointing out to your family if the movie's depiction of 'amnesia' or 'hallucinations' is medically accurate or just fake drama.
Feeling immense empathy for the innocent characters and wishing they had someone to talk to before things went wrong.
Analyzing the mastermind's brilliant planning, strategy, and how they manipulated the entire police system.

questions.scenario: A friend tells you a huge, dark secret they have been hiding from their strict parents.

options.text: Promise absolute confidentiality, hold their hand, and create a completely safe, non-judgmental space for them to cry.
Listen carefully, but mentally assess if their secret implies they are a physical or medical danger to themselves.
Gently encourage and prepare them to eventually tell a trusted adult or teacher when they are emotionally ready.
Help them formulate a strategic, step-by-step plan on how to reveal it to their parents to minimize the scolding.

questions.scenario: How do people in your tuition class generally describe you?

options.text: 'The deep thinker who gives the absolute best, most comforting emotional advice when someone is sad.'
'The science nerd who knows weird, fascinating facts about how the human brain and chemicals work.'
'The sweet, reliable, and patient friend that everyone naturally trusts and feels safe around.'
'The natural manager who keeps the group chat alive, organizes plans, and resolves all our friend-group drama.'

Clinical_Psychologist.title: The Mind Healer (Clinical Psychologist / Therapist)
Clinical_Psychologist.primary_match_text: You are highly empathetic, a fantastic listener, and naturally draw people in. You are not afraid of deep, dark emotions, and you want to help people heal from their internal traumas and mental health struggles.
Clinical_Psychologist.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a quiet, safe clinic, conducting 1-on-1 therapy sessions, helping clients process depression or anxiety, and teaching them healthy coping mechanisms.
Clinical_Psychologist.alternative_match_text: Your extreme empathy and listening skills would also make you a fantastic Life Coach, Social Worker, or Writer.
Clinical_Psychologist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities with Psychology is ideal). Degree: BA/B.Sc in Psychology. Next Steps: MA/M.Sc in Clinical Psychology, followed by an M.Phil recognized by the RCI (Rehabilitation Council of India) to get a license.

Psychiatrist.title: The Brain Doctor (Psychiatrist)
Psychiatrist.primary_match_text: You are analytical, scientific, and logical. You understand that mental health isn't just about feelings; it's about biology, brain chemistry, and medicine. You want to cure the brain using science.
Psychiatrist.day_in_the_life: Working in a hospital, diagnosing severe mental illnesses like Schizophrenia or Bipolar Disorder, studying brain scans, and prescribing the exact medications needed to balance brain chemicals.
Psychiatrist.alternative_match_text: Your love for human biology and the brain makes you a perfect fit for Neurology, Neuro-surgery, or Medical Research.
Psychiatrist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCB is strictly mandatory). Entrance: Crack NEET-UG. Degree: 5.5-year MBBS degree. Next Steps: Crack NEET-PG and pursue an MD in Psychiatry.

School_Counselor.title: The Trusted Guide (School Counselor / Child Psychologist)
School_Counselor.primary_match_text: You are approachable, patient, and incredibly warm. You love working with teenagers and children. You want to be the safe adult that you wish you had when you were growing up.
School_Counselor.day_in_the_life: Working in a vibrant school, helping students deal with bullying, exam stress, career confusion, and mediating meetings between angry teenagers and their parents.
School_Counselor.alternative_match_text: Your patience and ability to connect with youth would make you a brilliant Special Educator, Teacher, or Pediatrician.
School_Counselor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities preferred). Degree: BA/B.Sc in Psychology or Child Development. Next Steps: MA in Counseling Psychology or a PG Diploma in Guidance and Counseling.

Organizational_Psychologist.title: The Corporate Mind (Industrial/Organizational Psychologist)
Organizational_Psychologist.primary_match_text: You understand human psychology, but you apply it to systems, teams, and productivity. You are a natural leader who wants to figure out how to make large groups of people work together happily and efficiently.
Organizational_Psychologist.day_in_the_life: Working in top MNCs, designing employee wellness programs, resolving toxic workplace conflicts, interviewing top talent, and advising CEOs on how to keep their teams motivated.
Organizational_Psychologist.alternative_match_text: Your understanding of group dynamics and systems makes you a perfect fit for Human Resources (HR), Management Consulting, or Corporate Strategy.
Organizational_Psychologist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Commerce or Humanities preferred). Degree: BA in Psychology or BBA. Next Steps: MA in Industrial/Organizational Psychology or an MBA in Human Resource Management (HRM).
